summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after accidentally dislodging his left percutaneous nephrostomy tube, presenting with flank pressure and pain. He underwent successful placement of a new nephrostomy tube, which resolved the hydronephrosis. He was treated for a suspected urinary tract infection with antibiotics, though the urine culture was contaminated. His chronic kidney disease, now stage 5, was complicated by acute kidney injury and metabolic acidosis, both of which improved with supportive care. He also experienced opioid withdrawal due to interruption of his home pain regimen, which was managed symptomatically. He was discharged home with home health services, prescribed antibiotics, pain medications, and clear follow-up instructions with urology and nephrology.
